verified.exploit_entry_point: The public request adapter with the default middleware chain: FetchRequestAdapter.sendNoResponseContent / sendPrimitive, driven with a recording transport at the end of the chain, so the recorded headers are exactly what the library decided to send. The native-request hand-off (convertToNativeRequest) is driven with a caller-side transport that follows redirects unless the request opts out. Case values are literals in the test tables; no product code computes an expected value.
sites: packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:79-82 (the default scrub deletes only the canonical property names)
packages/http/fetch/src/fetchRequestAdapter.ts:529-532 (every header key is lower-cased before the scrub sees it)
packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/authorizationHandler.ts:53,67,80 (a supported configuration writes the same bearer token under the canonical spelling next to the lower-cased one)
packages/http/fetch/src/middlewares/options/redirectHandlerOptions.ts:60-62,89-92 (the roster documents Proxy-Authorization as out of scope)

packages/http/fetch/src/fetchRequestAdapter.ts:556-566 (the native-request hand-off returns an authenticated request with no redirect policy; the manual policy is set only by the middleware chain at redirectHandler.ts:175)
routes: T1: a cross-host, cross-port or cross-scheme redirect through the default chain, with the lower-cased header keys the adapter produces
T4: the same redirect when an authentication middleware has added a second, canonically spelled copy of the token
T5: the same redirect with a caller-attached proxy credential
T3 (coupled functional): the prepared native request stays authenticated with its method, body and headers
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own tests for the affected area, from pristine copies: test/node/RedirectHandler.ts, test/node/RedirectHandlerOptions.ts, test/node/kiotaClientFactory.ts, test/node/MiddlewareFactory.ts, test/node/httpClient.ts, test/common/middleware/authorizationHandler.ts and test/common/middleware/headersUtil.ts (63 tests), plus 10 hidden functional tests, on the pinned tree, the reference fix and every check patch; 73 functional tests in total.

traps.shape: the default scrub removes the credential headers by their canonical property names, but every key has already been lower-cased, so the delete is a no-op for every credential; the host/protocol comparison itself is already case-insensitive, which makes the guard look complete
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported example shows one redirect and the guard compares the origins correctly, so the deletion looks right
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-396q-4vc8-28x9) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: a supported authentication configuration writes the same bearer token under a second, canonically spelled header name, so a fix that matches only the lower-cased spelling still leaves the credential on the request
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the authentication middleware looks redundant because the adapter has already authenticated, and its presence check is a plain property read
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code reachable through the documented KiotaClientFactory authentication parameter

traps.shape: the scrub roster names only two of the three standard request credential headers; a caller-attached proxy credential is never removed, and the source comments argue the omission is intentional
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the comments state that proxy configuration is handled below JavaScript, so the header looks inapplicable
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the advisory's own remediation names Proxy-Authorization

traps.shape: the native-request hand-off returns the authenticated request with no redirect policy, so the caller's transport follows a cross-origin redirect and forwards the attached credentials; automatic redirect following is disabled only on the middleware path
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the hand-off is documented as returning a fully prepared request to the caller, so redirect policy looks like the caller's responsibility
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the public hand-off predates the advisory and the published fix did not touch it

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), instruction + the task image's /app only

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: the product's protection is to omit headers from a request that still completes; a refusal would fail the functional cross-origin completion test
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: an exception in the scrub is caught by the product and would leave the credentials in place, so it cannot pass as a refusal
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: no roles, peers or directions exist on this surface; every security case drives the same request path
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the operation is a request transform with no read/write or verb split
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: nothing looks up an authority or secret on this surface; the caller supplies every credential

history.summary: The default redirect scrub matches credential header names case-sensitively while the adapter lower-cases every key, so Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization survive a cross-origin redirect
